title: a kill in the window between ingest() returning and the .committed marker being written makes startup recovery restore the OLD rows over a complete new session (consistent, but the finished re-transcription/embedding work is discarded and must be paid for again)
evidence: reingest-crash.test.mjs 'kill after ingest returned but BEFORE the commit marker was written': recovery output is byte-identical to the pre-reingest state, new session removed. The window is one small atomic file write.
fix_direction: none needed for safety; to save the work, write the marker from inside ingest() before its last step, or have recovery compare the new session's turns/chunks to the Drive file and keep it when complete.

title: type exactness is proven only against the in-memory BSON-bytes fake: rows read through the real driver arrive with promoteValues defaults (int64 that fits -> JS number, double 5.0 -> JS number 5), so the snapshot maps them to Int32/Double by value and a replayed int64 or integral double can be stored as a different numeric BSON type than it had
evidence: typed() maps JS numbers to Int32 (int32 range integer) or Double; the scopedCollection accessor offers no promoteValues:false. Never run against a real MongoDB (hard rule). Vectors stored as BSON arrays of doubles with integral values (0.0, 1.0) would come back as Int32.
fix_direction: read snapshot rows with promoteValues:false through a scoped accessor option, or check on the local work-DB copy that the corpus has no int64 / integral-double fields before relying on replay.

title: recovery repairs database rows only: the old session's local data/toc-migrated/<old> directory (removed by finish() on success) and the failed attempt's data/toc-migrated/<new> files are not reconciled after a kill, and a Windows pid reused by an unrelated process makes a dead holder's lock look live until the 6 h stale limit
evidence: recoverSnapshot touches only scopedCollection rows; acquireReingestLock uses process.kill(pid, 0).
fix_direction: record the lock holder's start time and compare; list local dirs in the manifest and reconcile them in recovery.
